context.guidance: Move credentials and keys that protect Personal Data out of source files and configuration into a secret store or the runtime environment. Rotate any value that has already been committed, and exclude .env and key files from version control and build context. Restrict the secret store to the identities that need it, as Rule 6(1)(b) requires for the systems that hold Personal Data.

value.fix: Take the hard-coded key out of the source and configuration files. Load it when the app runs from an environment variable or a secret store, such as HashiCorp Vault, AWS Secrets Manager, GCP Secret Manager or Azure Key Vault. If the variable is missing, the app should stop at startup instead of falling back to a built-in default. Treat the committed value as exposed: rotate or revoke it now, and update everything that uses it. If you need to, remove it from git history with git filter-repo or BFG and force-push, but rotate it either way. Add .env, .env.*, *.pem, *.key and similar key files to .gitignore and .dockerignore so they stay out of version control and build contexts. Commit a .env.example file that has placeholder values only. Add secret scanning, such as gitleaks, trufflehog or GitHub secret scanning, as a pre-commit hook and in CI. Give secret-store access only to the service identities that need it, with least-privilege IAM and access logging, as Rule 6(1)(b) requires for systems holding Personal Data.
